issue.title: Replace the remaining multiprocessing-fork and os.fork sites in the test suite with in-process seams
issue.description:
Forking from a multi-threaded process inherits only the calling thread, so any lock or buffer another thread held at fork time is inherited in an indeterminate state. Under xdist every worker carries a live execnet receiver thread, so every fork in a test is a fork-after-threads hazard.

This is proven twice, not theoretical. It was the root cause of tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py::test_headless_epic_approval_submits_while_inflight_launch_holds_anchor (bead sase-nz), which accumulated 12 full-run failure records across six workspaces and twelve heads between 2026-08-06 and 2026-08-17 before b6246f1cf replaced the fork with an in-process flock holder. Task sase-o5 then removed the four fork sites in tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py the same way (epic sase-ns.6.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.6.4).

DISCOVERED BY: epic sase-ns.6.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.6.4, which recorded this as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP rather than widening its own scope. Re-verified on master 5e58fb1c8 by the epic's land agent:

  $ grep -rln 'get_context("fork")|os\\.fork\\(\\)' tests/
  tests/test_prompt_artifact_staging.py
  tests/test_procs_supervisor.py
  tests/logs/test_run_log.py
  tests/monitor/test_monitor_proc_facade.py
  tests/agents_sync/test_publication_outbox.py

(tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py no longer matches; a docstring in it names the retired pattern in prose.)

SCOPE: replace each site with an in-process seam that still exercises genuine contention, following the two model fixes:

- tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py::_foreign_epic_launch_lock_holder (b6246f1cf) -- a contextmanager that takes the same flock on the real lock path, writes the same holder-identity JSON production writes, and self-checks that a second open() is refused with BlockingIOError before yielding.
- tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py::_ForeignEpicLaunchLockWorker -- a thread worker that runs the production lock helper inside a fresh contextvars.Context, so the ContextVar re-entrancy guard does not short-circuit the real flock wait, and re-raises the worker's assertion instead of flattening it into an exit code.

Preserve exactly what each test asserts. These tests exist to prove real contention or real process behavior, so a replacement that only pretends to contend would silently retire their value. Some sites may genuinely need a separate process -- spawn-based multiprocessing, or subprocess, is a legitimate answer where the test is really about process boundaries (spawn does not inherit threads and is not this hazard). Where an in-process seam cannot express what a site needs, say so in the bead note rather than weakening the assertion.

VERIFICATION: no 'fork' multiprocessing context or os.fork() call remains in tests/ outside prose; each touched file passes serially, under just test-contention with SASE_CONTENTION_REPEAT=3, and in a full parallel lane; just install && just check green.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-o5 — the single-file predecessor of this task (tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py). Worked as phase sase-ns.6.6.6.4 of epic sase-ns.6.6.6; its landed diff is the nearest model for the thread-worker shape and is worth reading before starting.
